note: Take the homepage 'Targeted Solutions for Every Skin' tiles from a 40% overlay to 20%, matching /pages/skin-concerns. Malcolm's call, 2026-08-25. Unlike the concern page this is a real block SETTING, not injected CSS — image-link-blocks has overlay_color/overlay_opacity in its schema — so no custom-html is involved.

measured_legibility_problem.why_these_tiles_are_not_the_concern_page: Each carries its white link label ON the photograph, bottom-left, so the flat overlay was doing legibility work, not decoration. The label is 15px bold — below WCAG's 18.66px 'large text' threshold — so it needs 4.5:1, not 3:1.
measured_legibility_problem.method: Measured on the rendered page. Label boxes come from the DOM via a Range over each text node — NOT from pixel heuristics. Glyphs and their antialias halo are masked; the remaining ground gives median and 95th-percentile (the brightest thing the text sits on) contrast against pure white. Other opacities are derived by recovering the un-overlaid photo from the live 20% capture — (px - 0.2*26) / 0.8 — and recompositing, which is exact.
measured_legibility_problem.DO_NOT_locate_the_label_by_counting_brig: The first pass found the label band by counting near-white pixels per row inside each tile. On photographs of skin, specular highlights clear any such threshold, so the 'label band' came back as rows 179-471 — 292 rows, essentially the whole tile. Every contrast number from that pass was white-text-against-the-entire-photograph and was wrong (it reported 40% as marginal at 3.89-4.17 and 20% as 2.51-2.72). It also could not detect its own error: adding the scrim moved the median but not the 95th percentile, because the brightest 5% lived in the untouched top of the picture. The label is 19px tall at y=453; ask the DOM.

worst_case_contrast_at_the_real_label_bo.40 (what it was): Fine Lines 7.12, Firming 7.80, Repair 7.13 — comfortable. Brightening unmeasurable in that capture, hidden behind the newsletter popup.
worst_case_contrast_at_the_real_label_bo.20 flat (what was asked for): Firming 4.12, Repair 4.14, Brightening 6.44 — two marginal. Fine Lines could not be measured at all because there was no dark ground left to measure: 100% of its label box was too pale for 4.5:1. White on near-white.
worst_case_contrast_at_the_real_label_bo.20 + bottom scrim (live): Fine Lines 5.41, Firming 6.62, Repair 4.74, Brightening 10.49 — all four PASS, and the too-pale share of every label box falls to ~12%, which is the antialias halo itself, i.e. the floor.

measured_legibility_problem.conclusion: The flat overlay was the wrong lever — the value that makes the labels legible is the value that greys the photographs, which is the whole reason for going to 20%. A local scrim buys the contrast only where it is needed.

the_fix_a_local_scrim: Keep the flat overlay at 20% and add a gradient that only darkens the bottom of each tile, where the label lives — the standard editorial pattern. Verified live: every tile clears 4.5:1, worst 4.74:1, while the top half of every photograph keeps the bare 20% wash. Implemented by overriding the theme's own overlay pseudo-element rather than adding a competing layer: .content-over-media:before already paints the flat overlay at z-index 1 with a .2s transition, so the gradient is layered ON that same background, above rgb(var(--content-over-media-overlay)). Adding a separate ::after would have fought the z-index — the content div is also z-index 1 and later in tree order, so an ::after would paint on top of the label.
scoped_to_one_section: The homepage has a SECOND image-link-blocks section — find_serum, 'Find Your Perfect Product', four tiles at 50% overlay. It is untouched: Malcolm asked about the concern tiles. That is why the CSS is keyed to the skin_concerns section id and not to .shopify-section--image-link-blocks, which would have caught both.
undo: python3 scripts/patch-template.py --restore backups/index-20260825-140544.json --template templates/index.json — that stamp is the pre-change 40% state. NOT index-20260825-140846.json, which is the half-done 20%-without-scrim state and would leave the labels failing contrast.

settings.html:
<style>
  /* The concern tiles run a 20% flat overlay so the photographs stay alive.
     The white label needs more ground than that, but only where it sits, so
     the contrast is bought locally with a bottom scrim instead of globally
     by darkening the whole picture.

     Layered onto the theme's OWN overlay pseudo-element. Do not move this to
     an ::after: .content-over-media > .content is also z-index 1 and later in
     tree order, so an ::after would paint over the label itself. */
  #shopify-section-template--26275134079361__skin_concerns .content-over-media::before {
    background:
      linear-gradient(to top,
        rgb(0 0 0 / 0.48) 0%,
        rgb(0 0 0 / 0.36) 16%,
        rgb(0 0 0 / 0.12) 34%,
        rgb(0 0 0 / 0) 50%),
      rgb(var(--content-over-media-overlay));
  }
</style>
